originalTitle: Trump: New tariffs 'doing the same thing' as the ones struck down by Supreme Court
summary: President Trump dismissed fears his tariffs could hurt the economy — especially as affordability concerns have become a key issue of the 2026 midterm elections.
content:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday said new U.S. tariffs are functionally the same as the ones the Supreme Court struck down as illegal earlier this year.

"It's a shame that I have to go a harder way for the tariffs because the Supreme Court, in a very close decision, you know, ruled against me," Trump said in a Fox News interview.

"Now, I have other ways of doing the same thing, but it's a more cumbersome, you know, way of doing it," he said.

Trump's comments on tariffs came four days after a federal lawsuit accused his administration of using different statutes as a pretext to resurrect the global tariff regime that failed in the courts.

"Changing the statute doesn't change the law — and changing the stated rationale doesn't make an unlawful tariff lawful," Sara Albrecht, chairman and CEO of Liberty Justice Center, the legal nonprofit behind the lawsuit, said of Trump's latest remarks.

"This statement bolsters our argument," Albrecht told CNBC in an emailed statement. "The president's own words indicate that these tariffs are simply another, more cumbersome way of achieving the same result after the Supreme Court ruled against him."

Trump also told Fox that he would rather the U.S. leave its trilateral trade deal with Canada and Mexico than renegotiate it.

"I don't care. I mean, I don't really want to. I'd rather be independent," Trump said when asked if he was still looking to update the deal known as USMCA, which the U.S. this month decided not to renew .

"Here's the thing: Mexico and Canada need us. We don't need them. The deal is important for them. It's not important for us," he said.

The Canadian and Mexican embassies in the U.S. did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Trump's comment.

The president's trade remarks came as his administration's use of tariffs has ramped back up in recent weeks.

The Trump administration on Friday imposed tariffs between 10% and 12.5% on goods from more than 80 countries, on the grounds that those trade partners failed to effectively prohibit the use of forced labor.

Those duties, brought under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, came into effect just as Trump's worldwide 10% tariff hit its 150-day time limit and expired.

Trump announced that temporary tariff on Feb. 20, the same day the Supreme Court struck down his prior "liberation day" duties, which set a 10% near-global "reciprocal" baseline tariff and saddled dozens of countries with higher individualized rates.

All three of those tariff policies were brought using different statutory authorities. The lawsuit filed Friday argues that Trump's newest tariffs, while ostensibly aimed at addressing forced labor practices, are "designed to preserve substantially the same broad tariff regime that this Court and the Supreme Court have held Congress did not authorize."

A senior administration official, when asked in a call with reporters Thursday if the focus on forced labor is an excuse to reimpose "liberation day," claimed that Trump has prioritized the issue "for many years."

The official added that the timing of new tariffs — coming into force directly as the temporary ones lapsed — was chosen "to avoid complexity" and not intended as a replacement.

Trump in Tuesday's interview also dismissed fears that his tariffs, which are taxes on imported goods, could hurt the economy — especially as Americans' cost-of-living concerns become a central issue of the upcoming midterm elections.

"The tariffs have made this country a fortune," Trump said, while claiming that his use of them has helped stopped numerous wars. "These tariffs — it's the greatest thing," he said.

The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Trump's remarks.
chineseTitle: 特朗普：新关税与最高法院驳回的关税“做同样的事情”
chineseSummary: 特朗普总统驳斥了人们对他的关税可能损害经济的担忧——尤其是考虑到负担能力问题已成为 2026 年中期选举的关键问题。
chineseContent:
唐纳德·特朗普总统周二表示，美国新关税在功能上与最高法院今年早些时候裁定为非法的关税相同。

特朗普在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示：“遗憾的是，我必须对关税采取更强硬的态度，因为最高法院在一项非常接近的裁决中做出了对我不利的裁决。”

“现在，我有其他方法可以做同样的事情，但这是一种更麻烦的方法，”他说。

特朗普就关税发表评论四天前，一项联邦诉讼指控他的政府利用不同的法规作为借口，恢复在法庭上失败的全球关税制度。

诉讼背后的合法非营利组织自由司法中心董事长兼首席执行官萨拉·阿尔布雷希特在谈到特朗普的最新言论时表示：“改变法规并不会改变法律，改变既定的理由也不会使非法关税合法化。”

阿尔布雷希特在一份电子邮件声明中告诉 CNBC：“这一声明支持了我们的论点。” “总统自己的话表明，在最高法院对他做出不利裁决后，这些关税只是实现相同结果的另一种更麻烦的方式。”

特朗普还告诉福克斯，他宁愿美国放弃与加拿大和墨西哥的三边贸易协定，也不愿重新谈判。

当被问及是否仍在寻求更新名为 USMCA 的协议时，特朗普表示：“我不在乎。我的意思是，我真的不想这样做。我宁愿独立。”

“事情是这样的：墨西哥和加拿大需要我们。我们不需要他们。这笔交易对他们来说很重要。对我们来说并不重要，”他说。

加拿大和墨西哥驻美国大使馆没有立即回应 CNBC 对特朗普言论置评的请求。

总统发表贸易言论之际，他的政府最近几周加大了关税的使用。

特朗普政府周五对来自80多个国家的商品征收10%至12.5%的关税，理由是这些贸易伙伴未能有效禁止使用强迫劳动。

这些关税是根据 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条征收的，就在特朗普向全球征收 10% 的关税达到 150 天期限并到期之际生效。

特朗普于 2 月 20 日宣布了临时关税，同一天最高法院撤销了他之前的“解放日”关税，该关税设定了接近全球的 10% 的“互惠”基准关税，并使数十个国家承担了更高的个人税率。

所有这三项关税政策都是通过不同的法定机构提出的。周五提起的诉讼称，特朗普最新的关税虽然表面上旨在解决强迫劳动行为，但“旨在保留本法院和最高法院认为国会未授权的大致相同的广泛关税制度。”

周四，一名高级政府官员在与记者通话时被问及对强迫劳动的关注是否是重新设立“解放日”的借口时，他声称特朗普“多年来”一直优先考虑这个问题。

这位官员补充说，新关税的时间安排——在临时关税失效后立即生效——是为了“避免复杂性”，而不是为了替代关税。

特朗普在周二的采访中还驳斥了人们的担忧，即他的关税（即对进口商品征税）可能会损害经济——尤其是在美国人对生活成本的担忧成为即将到来的中期选举的核心问题的情况下。

特朗普说：“关税让这个国家发了财。”他同时声称，他对关税的使用帮助阻止了许多战争。 “这些关税——这是最伟大的事情，”他说。

美国贸易代表办公室没有立即回应 CNBC 对特朗普言论发表评论的请求。
